# Check: upstream keybindings.test.ts

## Upstream file
tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/test/keybindings.test.ts

## Subject
Keybindings manager — rebinding conflicts and default preservation.

## Upstream test count (approx)
3

## Behaviors asserted upstream
- does not evict selector confirm when input submit is rebound
- does not evict cursor bindings when another action reuses the same key
- still reports direct user binding conflicts without evicting defaults

## Upstream dependencies
KeybindingsManager, TUI_KEYBINDINGS from ../src/keybindings.js

## Upstream notes
Tests keybinding conflict detection and preservation of default bindings when user rebinds. getConflicts() returns array of {key, keybindings[]}.

## Candidate Elixir counterpart(s)
- apps/octo_pi_tui/test/octo_pi/tui/keybindings_test.exs

## Processing protocol
Same as standard check ticket protocol in epic opi-q5k description. Compliance ticket must list each missing behavior and require a post-implementation re-comparison. Block opi-q5k.1.

comments.text:
# Audit findings

Upstream: tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/test/keybindings.test.ts (3 assertions)
Ours: apps/octo_pi_tui/test/octo_pi/tui/keybindings_test.exs (13 tests across 5 describes)

The upstream file is narrowly focused on a single invariant: **user rebinds must not evict unrelated default bindings**. All three upstream tests verify this invariant in different shapes.

## MAPPED (partial only)

| Upstream | Elixir |
|---|---|
| "still reports direct user binding conflicts" (conflict detection half) | "detects user-introduced conflicts" |

## UNMAPPED

- **Upstream #1** "does not evict selector confirm when input submit is rebound": after rebinding `tui.input.submit` to ["enter", "ctrl+enter"], `tui.select.confirm` must still return ["enter"]. Elixir "user bindings override defaults" confirms the override takes effect but does NOT assert other bindings are preserved. **Gap: no-eviction-of-sibling invariant untested.**
- **Upstream #2** "does not evict cursor bindings when another action reuses the same key": rebinding `tui.select.up` to ["up", "ctrl+p"] must leave `tui.editor.cursorUp` at ["up"]. No Elixir equivalent. **Gap.**
- **Upstream #3** "still reports direct user binding conflicts without evicting defaults": the second assertion — that `tui.editor.cursorLeft` still returns ["left", "ctrl+b"] even while a conflict exists — has no Elixir equivalent. Elixir asserts conflict shape, not default preservation under conflict. **Gap.**

## N/A / EXTRA

Elixir adds API-surface tests (matches?/3, get_keys/2 unknown binding, set_user_bindings/2, no-conflicts baseline). Useful but not relevant to upstream scope.

## Action

All three upstream tests probe the same eviction invariant — creating one compliance ticket covering all three.
